<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

Here's a draft you can send:

---

Subject: Late fee on Unit 3B – payment received within grace period

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your note regarding the $75 late fee on Unit 3B. I've reviewed my payment records and my rent was submitted within the lease's grace period, so I'd like to dispute the charge.

Section 4.2 of the Maple Court lease states that rent is due on the 1st, that a grace period applies through the 5th, and that no late fees may be charged during the grace period. Since my payment was received on the 3rd, the fee doesn't appear to be consistent with the lease terms.

I'd appreciate it if you could remove the $75 late fee from my account. Please let me know if you need any documentation from me, such as a bank statement or payment confirmation showing the date the payment was sent. I'm happy to provide it.

Thank you for looking into this. I look forward to your confirmation.

Best regards,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

A couple of tips:
- Attach or reference your payment confirmation (the date the check was mailed, the portal receipt, or your bank record) so the dispute is easy to verify.
- Keep a copy of this email. Under Section 9.4, notices may be sent by email, so this counts as a written notice.

I'm happy to share proof of payment, such as a bank confirmation or receipt, if that would help. Thanks for looking into this.
